facts.fact_text: Following the February-March 2003 presidential election in Armenia, the applicant participated in a series of rallies of protest organised in Yerevan by the opposition parties.
On 7 April 2003 at 5 p.m. a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 took place on the Mashtots Avenue next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան).
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature.
During the demonstration of 7 April 2003, criticism of the Government and of the conduct of the presidential election was voiced.
The applicant took part in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the march that followed the demonstration of 7 April 2003.

The applicant alleged that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003 in order to facilitate its conduct.

The Government did not dispute the applicant's allegation that traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of the Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the march that followed the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
According to the applicant, at around 6 p.m. on 7 April 2003 she went to work.
According to the applicant, after work at around 9 p.m. on 7 April 2003 the applicant went home.
According to the applicant, on her way home on 7 April 2003 she was approached by three men in civilian clothes who, without presenting themselves, started dragging her to a nearby car.
According to the applicant, the three men who approached her on 7 April 2003 twisted her arms, punched her and pushed her into the car.
According to the applicant, she screamed and tried to resist when the three men in civilian clothes attempted to drag her to a nearby car on 7 April 2003.
The applicant was taken to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժին).
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the applicant found out that she had been arrested for having participated in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest (արձանագրություն բերման ենթարկելու մասին).
The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant had been "arrested at 7.30 p.m. at 12 Khorhurdneri Street for violating public order".
The applicant alleged that the time of her apprehension was not correctly recorded in the arrest record.
The applicant alleged that in reality she was arrested at 9 p.m. on 7 April 2003.

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that the applicant was brought to the Central District Police Station for having participated on 7 April 2003 in an unauthorised march headed from the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) to the Constitutional Court and violated public order.
The applicant was subjected to a search at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan following her arrest on 7 April 2003, during which no illegal items were found.
A record of the search of the applicant was drawn up following the search on 7 April 2003.
The police officers questioned the applicant following her arrest on 7 April 2003.
The applicant made a written statement (արձանագրություն բացատրություն վերցնելու մասին) in which she gave details of her participation in the demonstration of 7 April 2003 and the following march.
In her written statement of 7 April 2003, the applicant stated that the street traffic was obstructed when the march headed towards the building of the Constitutional Court.
In her written statement of 7 April 2003, the applicant stated that she was in the front line holding the Armenian flag and screaming "justice".
The applicant alleged that her written statement of 7 April 2003 was made under pressure and was dictated to her by the police officers.

The applicant alleged that while most of her written statement of 7 April 2003 was true, the part concerning the obstruction of traffic did not correspond to reality since the traffic had been beforehand suspended by the traffic police.

The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) in which it was stated that the applicant had "participated in a march and violated public order" on 7 April 2003.
The applicant's actions on 7 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – "the CAO") as minor hooliganism.
The record of an administrative offence relating to the events of 7 April 2003 was signed by the applicant.

The applicant put her signature in the section of the record of an administrative offence of 7 April 2003 certifying that she had been made aware of her rights under Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

In the section of the record of an administrative offence of 7 April 2003 marked as "other information relevant for the determination of the case", the applicant added "I do not wish to have a lawyer".
The applicant alleged that she was forced to sign the record of an administrative offence and other documents prepared by the police officers on 7 April 2003 under threat of violence.
The applicant alleged that the police officers persuaded her to refuse a lawyer on 7 April 2003 by insisting that a lawyer's involvement would not help and would only be detrimental to her case.

On 7 April 2003 at around 12 midnight the applicant was taken to Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan (Երևան քաղաքի Կենտրոն և Նորք-Մարաշ համայնքների առաջին ատյանի դատարան), who examined the case.
The Government contested the applicant's allegation that she was forced to sign documents under threat of violence on 7 April 2003.
According to the Government, the applicant was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan for two hours on 7 April 2003.
According to the Government, the applicant was taken to Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan at 9.30 p.m. on 7 April 2003.
According to the Government, the police officers explained to the applicant her right to have a lawyer on 7 April 2003 and advised her to avail herself of this right, which she did not wish to do.
According to the Government, the record of an administrative offence of 7 April 2003 was signed by the applicant voluntarily and without any objections.

According to the Government, the applicant failed to initiate any actions aimed at the defence of her rights on 7 April 2003, such as lodging motions or availing herself of other procedural rights guaranteed by Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO), despite having been made aware of them.

The materials of the applicant's administrative case arising from the events of 7 April 2003 were transmitted by the police to Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for examination.

The materials of the applicant's administrative case arising from the events of 7 April 2003 contained the following documents: (1) the record of an administrative offence; (2) the police report; (3) the record of the applicant's arrest; (4) the record of the search of the applicant; and (5) the applicant's written statement.
All documents in the applicant's administrative case arising from the events of 7 April 2003 were signed by the applicant except the police report.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to an administrative fine of 1500 Armenian drams (approximately EUR 2.4 at the material time) in relation to the events of 7 April 2003.

Judge M.'s entire finding in relation to the events of 7 April 2003 stated: "On 7 April 2003 between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. ... on the Mashtots Avenue [the applicant], together with a group of people, obstructed street traffic, violated public order by making a loud noise, and incited other participants of the demonstration to do the same..."
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, drawn up in calligraphic handwriting, the hearing was held in public with the participation of the judge, a clerk and the applicant.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the judge explained the applicant's rights to her and informed her of the possibility to challenge the judge and the clerk.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the applicant did not wish to lodge any challenges.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the applicant stated that she was aware of her rights and did not wish to have a lawyer.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the judge read out the motion submitted by the police, seeking to impose administrative liability on the applicant.

According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the applicant submitted that at 4.30 p.m. she had participated in a march which had taken place in the Central District of Yerevan, during which they had obstructed the traffic and invited other people to join them.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, no questions were put to the applicant.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the judge read out and examined the materials prepared by the police.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, having familiarised herself with the materials, the applicant accepted that she had signed the record of an administrative offence.
According to the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the judge departed to the deliberation room, after which he returned and announced the decision.

The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003 was a fake and was drafted at some point after the hearing in order to create an appearance of lawfulness.
The applicant alleged that in reality there was no clerk present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003 and the hearing was not being recorded.
The applicant alleged that the court hearing of 7 April 2003 lasted not more than five minutes and was conducted in Judge M.'s office.
The applicant alleged that, contrary to what the record stated, only Judge M., the applicant and the accompanying police officer were present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003.

The applicant alleged that the accompanying police officer at the court hearing of 7 April 2003 did not participate in the hearing and his functions were limited only to bringing the applicant before the judge.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. neither explained her rights nor asked whether she wanted to have a lawyer.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the materials of the case file were not read out and she was not allowed to make any oral submissions.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, no evidence was taken or examined.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. prepared the decision solely on the basis of the materials prepared by the police.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. threatened the applicant with imminent detention if she did not refrain from further participation in demonstrations.
